judgements.justification: In A, ecPK cut 6 to 5 on the wrong claim that subsampling amplification lets point queries take less noise, and WJWj's 5 cites a tightness doubt Theorem 4 answers; B's wrong claim (eGa2) was refuted and withdrawn.
B's AC argued only for acceptance and gave no reading for the spotlight; an unexplained tier is R30, not an argued override.
B's 8 (bo89) is a restated summary naming no weakness, and it was the only score above 7 behind the spotlight; A's 7 (dx3d) is also generic praise.
Both committees saw that Theorem 3 leans on [3]; the authors disclosed no flaw to one forum only.
No substantive flaw was learned and ignored; B's concession on proof originality concerned framing, which both committees knew.
Scores moved after the rebuttal in both committees (epzC up in A, eGa2 up in B).
The A-only issues that moved scores (mechanism specificity, tightness) were wrong, and B's correct one-metric point lowered nothing; no substantive concern split the committees.
Both saw the theory rests on Balcer and Vadhan [3]; WJWj (A) counted it as incremental, while 4cAR (B) kept a 7 after the authors conceded it.
Neither AC adopted one reviewer's position; A's AC accepted on its own view of significance.
No reviewer cited other reviews as the reason for a score change.
The authors answered every review within the response period; ecPK's late objection was not a follow-up the authors misread or skipped.
WJWj (A, 2 hours) alleged undefined terms without examples, never replied, and his 5 counted; bo89 (B) left only '[response acknowledged]' and his 8 counted.
Neither AC recommended below its reviewers' majority; both accepted.
A's AC accepted on its own judgement despite a 5.75 mean, not by a threshold.
ecPK's and WJWj's objections concern the generality and tightness of the main result, not a peripheral point.
Both committees read the paper as a theory result for official statistics.
epzC raised on clarifications but did not state the core was outside his expertise.
WJWj's request for practical implications was a minor point; the committees did not apply different bars to the paper type.
bo89's praise is thin but rests on no checkable wrong claim.
ecPK did not accept the group-privacy answer and lowered rather than kept his score; WJWj never acknowledged an answer.
Neither committee is recorded refusing or crediting promised revisions in a way that moved its tier.
Every stated change of position matched a score edit.
No off-record reviewer appears in either committee.
WJWj's clarity complaint gives no examples and no expertise gap with B's reviewers is recorded.
No reviewer raised a score silently against his own text.
A's AC accepted over both 5s on significance, not by discounting the silent WJWj, and B had no silent detractor.
B's 8 is a thin summary, not a detailed checked reading, so no invested champion is present.
No reviewer admitted reading only part of the paper; ecPK's unfamiliarity with the proof technique is not partial reading.
No reviewer contested the premise from another theoretical tradition.
B's meta-review ends 'I recommend that the paper be accepted' and gives no reason for the spotlight on scores of 8, 7, 6, 6.
B's literature-aware reviewer (eGa2) made a wrong subsumption claim and conceded; neither committee checked baselines against published results.
A's meta-review calls the reviews divided, which the record supports; repeating ecPK's doubt is not misstating positions.
No one raised a narrow-audience concern.
A's late ecPK review misread Theorem 3's scope and A's AC argued acceptance against a divided panel without weighing a higher tier, while B, whose wrong objection was withdrawn, gave a spotlight.
No new experiments were posted to one forum only.
B's high-confidence reviewer (eGa2) rated lowest after a wrong objection, and A had no high-confidence expert outscored by less-informed reviewers.

added.name: Late post-response objection stood unanswered
added.definition: A reviewer in one committee added a new objection and changed their score after the author response period had closed, so the authors could not answer it and it entered the decision unrebutted, while the other committee's objections were raised in time to be answered.
added.justification: R01 covers a wrong claim driving a score but not the timing that denied the authors any reply; R11 concerns authors misreading or skipping a reply they could give; R20 concerns a kept score. None names an objection added after the response window that therefore stood unrebutted.

reasoning: Both committees accepted the paper for its importance to official statistics; the tier gap comes from A's two weak 5s and B's thin 8 plus an unexplained spotlight. In A, ecPK's wrong subsampling claim and WJWj's tightness doubt (answered by Theorem 4) held scores down (R01), WJWj's thin, silent review counted (R12), and the misreading detractor left the AC arguing only acceptance (R34). ecPK's objection arrived a month after the author response, so no one answered it and the meta-review echoed it; no existing reason names that timing, so R37 was added. In B, bo89's summary-only 8 (R03, R12) and an AC spotlight with no stated case (R30) lifted the tier. The shared reliance on [3] counted against the paper only in A (R08).
